item.text:
<linkedin_post>Wikipedia depends on published sources as well as the volunteers who turn those sources into articles. The Wikimedia Foundation wants courts weighing AI copyright cases to consider what happens to that supply of source material.

In a brief filed in the OpenAI copyright litigation, the Foundation warns that a blanket finding of fair use could encourage publishers to close off content, leaving less material available to Wikipedia editors and other readers. It also warns that an overly restrictive ruling could limit the development of tools that benefit open-source projects.

Wikimedia proposes treating model training differently from retrieval-augmented generation. It argues that training can qualify as fair use when the resulting model is new and different from its sources, while companies using copyrighted works to ground chatbot answers should follow publishers’ licensing terms.</linkedin_post>
